title: Career Aptitude Profile
shortDescription: Maps your Brain Profile strengths and interests against career directions likely to suit how you think.
longDescription: Career Aptitude Profile is built on Holland's RIASEC model — the theoretical basis for the U.S. Department of Labor's O*NET Interest Profiler and one of the most widely used frameworks in career counseling. It measures interest across six vocational types: Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, and Conventional. Your highest-scoring types (your "Holland code") point toward career directions that tend to fit how you like to work.
sourceNote: Original self-report items written to implement Holland's published RIASEC structure (Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, Conventional) — the O*NET Interest Profiler itself (and its exact item wording) is a U.S. Department of Labor instrument with its own copyright/attribution terms, so its actual items are not reproduced here; this uses the same six-type theoretical model with original statements. Deliberately excluded from the Brain Profile aggregate: RIASEC measures vocational interest, not cognitive ability, so it isn't comparable to the other assessments' dimension scores the way Palmistry is excluded for a different reason (no real scoring at all).

scoringDimensions.label: Interest Engagement
scoringDimensions.description: Overall engagement across all six RIASEC types — how strongly you responded across the board, not which type dominates.

scoringDimensions.label: Realistic
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in hands-on, mechanical, physical work.

scoringDimensions.label: Investigative
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in analytical, scientific, research-oriented work.

scoringDimensions.label: Artistic
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in creative, expressive, design-driven work.

scoringDimensions.label: Social
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in helping, teaching, supporting roles.

scoringDimensions.label: Enterprising
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in leading, persuading, business-oriented work.

scoringDimensions.label: Conventional
scoringDimensions.description: Interest in organized, detail-oriented, structured work.

resultRanges.title: Undifferentiated Profile
resultRanges.description: Your interest ratings were fairly flat across all six types — none stood out strongly. That's not a bad result; it can mean genuinely broad interests, or that none of these six categories captures what motivates you. Check the six scores above for your closest lean.
recommendations: Look at your two or three highest-scoring types above, even if none feels dominant — that pairing is still informative
Try activities from your highest type or two to see if engagement follows
Retake this after trying a few different kinds of work or projects

resultRanges.title: Mildly Differentiated
resultRanges.description: A modest lean toward one or two RIASEC types. Look at your highest-scoring dimensions above for your closest career direction.
recommendations: Explore roles that combine your top one or two types
Notice which specific items you rated highest — the activity itself may matter more than the category

resultRanges.title: Differentiated Profile
resultRanges.description: A clear lean toward specific RIASEC types is visible above. Your highest-scoring one or two types form your Holland code.
recommendations: Research career paths associated with your top two types (e.g. Investigative + Artistic often points toward research or design-adjacent fields)
Weigh your Holland code alongside your Brain Profile's cognitive strengths for a fuller picture

resultRanges.title: Strongly Differentiated
resultRanges.description: Your interests are clearly concentrated in a small set of RIASEC types — a strong, well-defined Holland code.
recommendations: A strongly differentiated profile like yours tends to predict clearer career satisfaction in matching fields
Seek out roles or projects that lean heavily into your top type specifically, not just adjacent ones

resultRanges.title: Highly Concentrated Profile
resultRanges.description: A very sharply defined interest profile — your top type (or two) stands well above the rest.
recommendations: This level of clarity is a strong signal — prioritize roles squarely in your top type over ones that only partially fit
Consider whether your current path actually uses your top type, or whether it's worth a deliberate shift
